agent_notes: The verb switches from first person singular (מֶנִּי 'than me') to plural (פְּשָׁעֵינוּ 'our transgressions'). Radak and Meiri read the 'I' as the people speaking as one; I keep the switch visible. STEPBible glosses מֶנִּי as 'for me'; I corrected it to 'than me' (comparative min after גבר, 'too strong for me'). Malbim's reading that the iniquities themselves 'speak' (דברי as 'words/things of') is noted, not adopted.

The syntax of תִּבְחַר וּתְקָרֵב is a relative clause without אשר (Ibn Ezra); the switch to 'we' in נִשְׂבְּעָה is the congregation answering. I render the cohortative 'may we be satisfied' per the STEPBible morphology (Vqc1cp); KJV 'we shall be satisfied' reads it as a future. Targum differs sharply (the righteous say 'we are satisfied').

מִבְטָח 'trust' is in apposition to אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׁעֵנוּ; KJV 'who art the confidence' adds a relative. Malbim's historical gloss tying נוראות to the Gibeonite affair (2 Sam 21) is his own and I mention it only as a minority reading.
